fullText:
Today, we’re sharing a look at our expanded system for monitoring frontier models at OpenAI, which in September helped us catch a model’s attempt to access the live internet during training.

Since the Hugging Face incident—when models broke out of an internal cybersecurity investigation where we weren’t running our misalignment monitors—we’ve substantially expanded our monitoring of frontier agents. We now monitor all frontier reinforcement learning runs and evaluations, as well as all internal Codex use. When our system finds evidence of a problem that might require intervention, it rapidly alerts human responders who can investigate and take action.

To detect when a model’s behavior departs from what we intended, we use several layers of monitoring. Activation probes look for patterns in a model’s internal activity. Reviewer models examine its reasoning and tool use, and investigative agents can read back through the model’s entire transcript to understand how a sequence of actions fits together and whether it warrants human review.

To test whether our current system would have detected the Hugging Face incident, we replayed the recorded activity with our new monitors in place. In the replay, our monitors alerted our security team about 30 minutes after the agents escaped their sandbox. That was more than 30 hours before the point at which the agents breached Hugging Face’s systems in the original incident.

In September, a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to reach the live internet. Our monitors flagged the breach within 15 minutes, and a responder began reviewing the alert three minutes later. The alert enabled responders to investigate while the run was still underway.

As we give models more autonomy, we need to know when they cross a boundary we expected to hold. We believe that monitoring is essential to catching those failures in time for people to intervene.

fullText:
Impressive NVIDIA paper on cutting agent costs.

For long-horizon agent tasks, you want the capable model for the early steps and a cheaper model for the rest. Handing off in the other direction saves little or nothing.

AgentBaton learns when to make that one switch from patterns in task progress. Each check has a median latency of 338 ms on one H100.

Across 11 model pairs and two benchmarks, it cuts API cost by 65.9% on average while largely keeping accuracy. Some pairs gain up to 8.8 points over running the capable model alone.

The handoff happens once per task, so it is easy to add to an existing agent loop.

If your agent bills are dominated by a frontier model, you might want to test one capable-to-cheap handoff before building a full router.

G. H. Hardy went to visit Srinivasa Ramanujan, who was ill, in London. Making conversation, Hardy said the taxi he came in had a rather dull number: 1729.

"No," said Ramanujan. "It is a very interesting number. It is the smallest number expressible as the sum of two cubes in two different ways."

1729 = 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³

Hardy told this story himself. Mathematicians still call 1729 the "Hardy–Ramanujan number", and numbers like it "taxicab numbers".

fullText:
Fascinating paper from MIT Media Lab on coordination in large agent societies.

(bookmark it)

I've seen a lot of success with agent-to-agent messaging recently.

That's exciting. I think agent persistence and coordination will unlock more novel use cases.

The authors report that with push delivery, an agent leading 20 negotiations proposes options that were already rejected 97% of the time. Its context fills up fast, and it drops the oldest replies.

The alternative they study is a pull-based inbox. Messages wait outside the context, and each agent's own rules decide what it reads and keeps.

In simulations of 1,000 to 16,000 LLM agents under noisy traffic, first-come-first-read misses every request. An inbox that first reads messages carrying a refundable deposit still finds about 60% of the agents a request needs, at every size.

Each inbox sets four rules. They decide what the agent reads, what it keeps, what a sender pays, and what a reply may say.

For multi-agent systems under load, you want to design the reading rules as carefully as the delivery protocol.

fullText:
Lower cost per task doesn’t always come from lower token prices.

On Agent Arena, GPT-6.1 Sol (Max) by @OpenAI costs $1.91 per task:
- 85% less than #1 Claude Opus 5.5 (Max) by @AnthropicAI at $12.51
- 87% less than #3 GPT-6 Astra (Max) by @OpenAI, at $14.93

But these savings come from different places.

Against Astra, Sol’s cost advantage comes primarily from lower token prices. Against Opus, it comes primarily from using fewer tokens per task.

How do we derive this?

Agent Arena tracks real costs of users’ tasks. Cost per task is the tokens a model uses times the price of each token, across input, output and cache-read tokens. By comparing pricing and token counts, we can identify what drives the cost reductions.

fullText:
红果日活 1.68 亿、人均每天两小时：秦朔说“字节时间”来了，程苓峰说这才刚开始

同一份数据，两篇文章，两个结论。野村证券 9 月的报告援引 QuestMobile 数据：今年 7 月，在中国使用时长排前 50 的 App 里，抖音第一次超过微信，字节系合计占 40.9%，腾讯系占 29.1%。

《第一财经日报》原总编辑秦朔据此写了《可怕的红果与中国互联网的字节时间》，担心红果这类算法机器正在吃掉人们的时间。

公众号“神在吗”的作者程苓峰 10 月 28 日接着写了《肉鸡时间》，认为份额只是表面，AI 短剧才是真正的“核爆”。两篇文章都在传的“红果年入 400 亿”，红果官方已经声明不实。

【红果有多能占时间】

秦朔引用的报告显示，红果 7 月日活 1.68 亿，一年翻了一倍，超过腾讯视频、爱奇艺、优酷、芒果 TV 四家相加（约 1.55 亿，未去重）。按使用总时长，红果已是中国第四大 App，排在抖音、微信、抖音极速版之后；今年 2 月人均每天看 125 分钟，比抖音和微信还长。

用户数上红果还差得远：微信日活 9 亿多，抖音 7 亿多。红果赢的是每个人花在上面的时间。

【秦朔：红果是一台时间吸收器】

秦朔把红果跑得快归结为四点。

1. 算法：每集 1 到 3 分钟，集集结尾留悬念，手指一滑就是下一集。

2. 供给：广电总局公布，今年前 8 个月全国上线微短剧 43 万部，是去年全年的 13 倍，其中 AI 剧超过九成。

3. 生态：在抖音刷到剧情片段，一键跳到红果看全集；番茄小说提供原著，秦朔文中说，去年的爆款短剧六成以上改编自番茄小说。

4. 免费：看剧不花钱，只看广告，平台拿广告收入给创作者分账。

腾讯刚在微信小程序里推出“绿泡泡短剧”应战，秦朔不看好。

秦朔打了个比方：字节所有 App 共用一套算法底座，像同一个酒瓶倒出不同的酒；腾讯靠社交起家，各个产品各用各的瓶子。秦朔还提到，在抖音和红果上看什么，朋友不知道，也就没有发朋友圈那种顾虑。

秦朔最在意代价。每天 125 分钟，意味着读书、思考、陪家人的时间少了。

秦朔预计短剧会分化成 K 型：底层是海量 AI 爽剧，顶层是少量真人精品，夹在中间的真人短剧最难过。秦朔也认为，时间多不等于价值高，腾讯在精品内容和中老年用户上仍有底盘。

刹车已经出现。9 月 1 日起施行的《微短剧发展管理办法》要求 AI 内容逐集标注，禁止平台用诱导沉迷的算法。红果 10 月 21 日宣布下线“看剧赚金币”：11 月 1 日起新用户不再有这个功能，12 月 31 日前全部下线，已攒下的金币和余额不受影响。

【抖音的反驳】

抖音集团副总裁李亮两次在微博回应，说“字节时间”不严谨：数据只算前 50 个 App，没算长尾 App 和电脑端；字节系最新的 41.8% 也没过半；短剧和短视频是充分竞争的行业，没有谁能一直第一。

秦朔 10 月 28 日回应说，“字节时间”是对注意力流向的概括，并非垄断认定。

【程苓峰：要看速度，AI 短剧是另一种东西】

程苓峰认为份额过没过半不重要。一年前字节系和腾讯系差不到 3 个点，现在差 13 个点，跑得快的一方会吸走所有新增的时间。

程苓峰把红果的优势叫作“三低合一”：番茄小说的网文省了剧本成本，字节的视频生成模型 Seedance 省了拍摄和演员成本，抖音流量便宜还能先放片段试水，省了拉新成本。

秦朔和程苓峰都看了穿越剧《持械入宋》。

秦朔说它比以前的短剧多样，有内涵也有专业性，但耗时、容易陷进去。程苓峰在里面看出了一场创业：主角用现代知识造火炮、改弩机，为了拿到铁料去考科举，再一点点组织人手，按未来的地图改造旧世界。

程苓峰还刷到讲急诊分诊、大闸蟹养殖、货车司机生活的剧，觉得这些短剧像一部百科全书。

所以程苓峰主张把真人短剧和 AI 短剧分开看。抖音的内容是普通用户拍的，短而散，算法负责把内容送到你面前；AI 短剧是一个懂行的编剧加 AI 拍出来的，一季上百集，往一个行业越挖越深，AI 用在把内容做出来。

程苓峰预计下一步 AI 两头都管：内容生成得比人看得快，每个人看到的剧情都不一样，广告直接编进情节。

到那时会分成两条路：
1. 免费的娱乐加广告，普通观众毫无招架之力，程苓峰称之为“肉鸡”；
2. 收费的教育，因材施教，逼人往上走。

【两人的分歧】

秦朔认为监管和金币下线会让红果从狂奔回到常规，短剧也不会杀死长内容，就像方便面没有取代正餐。程苓峰认为这才是“核爆当夜”，引用朋友的话说“字节没有上限”。

两人都担心沉迷。秦朔担心的是人的注意力和耐心被算法重塑；程苓峰担心的是社会更加 K 型，少数人借 AI 往上走，多数人被娱乐吞掉。

【数字靠不靠得住】

字节系、腾讯系的时长份额有出处，来自野村报告援引的 QuestMobile 数据，7 月是 40.9% 对 29.1%（秦朔引用），8 月是 41.8% 对 28.6%（程苓峰引用），统计范围只有前 50 个 App。

红果“第四大 App”“人均 125 分钟”出自同一份第三方报告，红果官方没有确认。

“前 8 个月 43 万部、AI 剧超九成”是广电总局网络视听司司长王小亮在国新办发布会上公布的。

程苓峰文中“红果今年收入 400 亿”，红果 10 月 27 日晚已声明不实，并称网传的机构数据和专家预计都不是官方信息。

拿来对比的“电影总票房 520 亿”是 2025 年全年数字，国家电影局公布为 518.32 亿元。

fullText:
Introducing Samaya Sterling, our new model post-trained for challenging financial research that outperforms the frontier! Sterling started off as a two person research effort to see if we could increase efficiency in agentic orchestration. To our surprise we were able to post-train a much smaller model (Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters) to greater accuracy (58.9% vs 55.9% on FrontierFinance) and 11x lower cost ($0.61 vs $6.89) than Claude Fable 5.1, the best performing frontier model.

We did this via a four-stage training process, two stages of SFT where the model first learns to research with our financial tools and how to construct a good agentic research strategy. The second two stages are RL, with an offline GRPO stage where the model further hones its research strategy from eight teachers that provide diverse approaches, and an online GRPO stage where the model can make end to end attempts and learn from its mistakes.

We see substantial gains from the co-adaptation of the model and harness through post-training, both through the model learning to effectively use the high-quality financial tools, and better compaction approaches that let even a small model execute on longer and deeper research.

We are exploring multiple follow-up directions, from multi-agent research swarms using this small model, to training firm-specific models to encode unique judgement, to training a larger model, where early results show even greater gains from the training process.
